title: Machine-learning-assisted materials discovery using failed experiments
research_question: Can failed experiments inform discovery?
negative_definition: Four-level crystal outcome collapsed to binary: score 1 (no solid) and 2 (amorphous solid) = failure; 3 (polycrystalline) and 4 (single crystal) = success; separate purity score captures multiphase versus single phase.
data_source: Archived laboratory notebooks; 3,955 complete reactions after incomplete entries were excluded
method: SVM trained on reaction/chemical descriptors; 15 historical train-test splits; prospective model-guided versus human-guided experiments on 34 previously untested diamines
validation_or_evaluation: 74% average historical split accuracy; prospective crystal-formation success 89% model-guided vs 78% human-guided, reported p<0.05 for two-sample proportion comparison
main_finding: A deliberately maintained experimental record of failed hydrothermal syntheses supported prediction and prospective synthesis; data entry was reported at about 50 reactions/hour and a 100-reaction audit found 1.89% field errors.
limitation_or_gap: One materials system; internally recorded lab-notebook outcomes, not extraction from published molecular-science literature. Binary failure merges no-solid and amorphous-solid outcomes. Prospective test was exploitation and not directly comparable to historical exploration split. Exact historical failure count not independently recomputed because official CSV download returned 403.
relevance_to_janus: Strong adjacent precedent for utility of experimental failures and value of preserving context; does not establish literature-mining novelty, cross-domain portability, or bioactivity-negative benefit

title: Hidden bias in the DUD-E dataset leads to misleading performance of deep learning in structure-based virtual screening
research_question: Do constructed negative examples create hidden benchmark bias?
negative_definition: decoys treated as inactive or non-binding
data_source: DUD-E; constructed actives and decoys
method: CNN and ligand-topology controls
validation_or_evaluation: cross-target and ligand-only tests
main_finding: High performance could be explained by analogue or decoy bias rather than learned molecular recognition
limitation_or_gap: focuses on benchmark bias, not recovery of omitted experimental observations
relevance_to_janus: Supports strict evaluation and cautions against using synthetic decoys as equivalent to measured negatives

title: DEEPScreen: high performance drug-target interaction prediction with convolutional neural networks using 2-D structural compound representations
research_question: How can negative selection and chemical bias be reduced in activity datasets?
negative_definition: experimentally measured inactive compounds
data_source: ChEMBL binding assays; MUV; DUD-E
method: dataset filtering plus CNN and scaffold or temporal splits
validation_or_evaluation: non-random splits and comparison across benchmark datasets
main_finding: Constructed target-specific datasets from measured activity records and explicitly examined negative selection bias; treated DUD-E as problematic
limitation_or_gap: filtering choices define inactivity and do not solve reporting or publication bias
relevance_to_janus: Useful precedent for measured negatives and leakage-aware splits

title: Chemical property prediction under experimental biases
research_question: Can models compensate for biased experimental sampling?
negative_definition: not a negative-data study; biased observation probability
data_source: QM9; ZINC; ESOL; FreeSolv with simulated sampling bias
method: inverse propensity scoring and causal representation learning with GNNs
validation_or_evaluation: comparison with an uncorrected baseline across simulated bias scenarios
main_finding: Bias mitigation improved most tasks and scenarios but was not fully stable
limitation_or_gap: bias was simulated; the study did not identify or recover missing negative observations
relevance_to_janus: Provides a model-side comparison framework, but not the central Janus contribution

title: Benchmarking compound activity prediction for real-world drug discovery applications
research_question: How should compound activity models be evaluated under real-world assay structure?
negative_definition: active or inactive activity labels within assay context
data_source: ChEMBL assays grouped by target, measurement type, condition, and source
method: CARA benchmark; assay categorization; zero-shot and few-shot settings
validation_or_evaluation: assay-level splits; per-assay metrics; VS versus LO tasks
main_finding: Real-world activity data are sparse and heterogeneous; global evaluation can overestimate performance; label distributions and measurement effects vary by assay
limitation_or_gap: benchmark addresses evaluation realism but does not mine unstructured negative evidence
relevance_to_janus: Important baseline for downstream evaluation and for preserving assay context

title: InertDB as a generative AI-expanded resource of biologically inactive small molecules from PubChem
research_question: Can curated/generated inactive compounds improve activity prediction relative to random-source negatives, property-matched decoys, or the benchmark's own measured inactives?
data_source: 3,205 PubChem-curated inactive compounds (CIC) plus 64,368 generatively produced compounds (GIC); GIC are synthetic candidates, not measured observations
method: PubChem assay outcomes for CIC; generative model trained on CIC for GIC; LIT-PCBA and MUV benchmark tests
validation_or_evaluation: NLP-assisted curation and generative expansion; ECFP4 random forest with identical holdout tests and 100 random splits; compared CIC/GIC, random PubChem/ZINC negatives, DeepCoy decoys, and separate replacement test against benchmark verified inactives
main_finding: Compared with random-source negatives/DeepCoy, CIC/GIC improve AUROC/MCC/balanced accuracy in some settings; replacing original verified inactives yields no significant change on LIT-PCBA (CIC p=.52; GIC p=.85), while MUV CIC shows a small significant gain (p=.0032)
limitation_or_gap: Strong precedent for a negative-compound resource and for source/chemical-space matching; generated GIC are not observed negatives, CIC are broad curated inactives rather than target-assay-specific measured negatives, and replacement results do not show a consistent gain over the benchmark's own verified inactives
relevance_to_janus: Critical novelty check: Janus cannot claim first inactive resource or that more negatives universally improve models; remaining gap is whether source-linked, newly recovered, assay-specific negatives add value beyond matched existing measured inactives and beyond data-volume/class-balance effects

title: Coverage bias in small molecule machine learning
research_question: Do common datasets cover known molecular structure space adequately?
negative_definition: not a negative-data study; missing structural coverage
data_source: widely used small-molecule datasets and known biomolecular structures
method: MCES-based coverage measure plus heuristic and optimization methods
validation_or_evaluation: coverage comparisons across datasets and structure space
main_finding: Many datasets lack uniform coverage, which can limit generalization to underrepresented compound classes
limitation_or_gap: coverage is structural and distributional; it does not establish publication bias or missing failed results
relevance_to_janus: Supports a broader representativeness dimension for AI-readiness

title: From text to insight: large language models for chemical data extraction
research_question: How should LLM-based chemical extraction pipelines be designed and evaluated?
negative_definition: qualitative or quantitative observations in unstructured text; negative evidence discussed as a literature bias
data_source: scientific papers, tables, figures, and supplementary information
method: LLM extraction workflow review and evaluation guidance
validation_or_evaluation: precision, recall, false positives, false negatives, ground truth, and domain validation
main_finding: There is growing extraction capability but no settled end-to-end evaluation framework; literature is biased toward positive and curated results
limitation_or_gap: review-level source; not a dedicated negative-result extraction benchmark
relevance_to_janus: Methodological foundation for evidence-grounded extraction and human verification

title: AI-readiness Criteria for Biomedical Data
research_question: What properties make biomedical data suitable for reliable AI use?
negative_definition: not a negative-data study; provenance and characterization requirements
data_source: Bridge2AI datasets and metadata
method: criteria and machine-actionable metadata framework
validation_or_evaluation: multidimensional readiness assessment across FAIRness, provenance, characterization, ethics, explainability, sustainability, and computability
main_finding: AI-readiness is context-dependent and extends beyond class balance or basic FAIRness
limitation_or_gap: biomedical framework; adaptation to molecular assay data is still required
relevance_to_janus: Provides the metadata and provenance lens for Janus schema design

title: The pursuit of accurate predictive models of the bioactivity of small molecules
research_question: What data and evaluation issues limit bioactivity prediction?
negative_definition: inactive compounds and data imbalance discussed as dataset composition issues
data_source: ChEMBL and common bioactivity datasets
method: review and synthesis of data-quality and modeling issues
validation_or_evaluation: comparison of dataset diversity, imbalance, chemical space, and applicability concerns
main_finding: Highlights dataset diversity, activity imbalance, and chemical-space coverage as recurring concerns
limitation_or_gap: review does not itself construct or validate a negative-evidence resource
relevance_to_janus: Useful map of adjacent bioactivity literature and terminology

title: Target prediction utilising negative bioactivity data covering large chemical space
research_question: Does adding large-scale negative bioactivity data improve target prediction?
negative_definition: PubChem assay records annotated inactive plus ChEMBL compounds selected as presumed inactive by sphere exclusion
data_source: ChEMBL18 active bioactivities and PubChem inactive records; 206,559,765 ligand-target pairs across 1,080 target-class models, with ~11 million presumed-inactive samples added for sparse classes
method: Bernoulli Naive Bayes with 2048-bit ECFP4; compare inactivity-inclusive models against active-only ChEMBL models
validation_or_evaluation: fivefold stratified CV; external WOMBAT test with 65,123 active compounds/418 target classes; Wilcoxon paired comparison of PR-AUC and BEDROC
main_finding: Authors report mean PR-AUC 0.56 vs 0.45 and BEDROC 0.85 vs 0.76 for negative-inclusive vs active-only models; Wilcoxon p=4.96e-05 and 7.08e-08 respectively. For 20 targets with >1,000 confirmed inactives, sphere-exclusion additions improved WOMBAT precision in 19 cases
limitation_or_gap: Important direct value precedent, but the negative-inclusive system mixes assay-annotated PubChem inactive with ~11M sphere-exclusion presumed negatives; external WOMBAT has no confirmed inactives and treats unannotated pairs as inactive; the activity-only comparator is ChEMBL-only rather than a tightly sample-size/coverage-matched ablation. Does not test contextual literature recovery or isolate the causal contribution of measured negatives
relevance_to_janus: Very high relevance: closes the broad claim that negative bioactivity data have never improved molecular target prediction; the defensible gap is evidence-type-specific, matched ablation of experimentally observed vs presumed vs recovered negatives, with provenance and assay context

title: Ligand biological activity predicted by cleaning positive and negative chemical correlations
research_question: Can high-quality negative data help separate activity-related chemical signals from undersampling noise?
negative_definition: high-quality negative data; exact source and construction require full-text review
data_source: chemical activity data from a drug-discovery setting
method: random-matrix-inspired statistical framework
validation_or_evaluation: modeling and analysis of active-negative chemical correlations
main_finding: Combines negative data with a statistical cleaning framework to identify differences between active and inactive molecules
limitation_or_gap: accepted-version metadata and full publication details need confirmation before relying on specific performance claims
relevance_to_janus: Shows that negative data have been used for chemical signal discovery, not only binary classification

title: ECBD: European chemical biology database
research_question: Can an open infrastructure preserve complete screening-pipeline activity data with per-compound outcomes and assay context?
negative_definition: Submitter-defined per-compound assay call can be active
data_source: inconclusive
method: inactive
validation_or_evaluation: error
main_finding: or undefined; numerical endpoints are retained separately and must not be collapsed indiscriminately
limitation_or_gap: EU-OPENSCREEN screening and bioprofiling projects; 107,414 compounds; paper's Aug 2024 snapshot: 89 submissions (48 public), 4.32M endpoints and 2.40M result values overall
evidence_level: FAIR repository with controlled compound/assay/target objects
relevance_to_janus: assay-context ontologies
column17: Retains positive and negative calls across primary/confirmatory/counter screens with endpoints and detailed assay metadata; validated confirmatory results can also be shared with ChEMBL
column18: Strong counterexample to any claim that contextualized molecular negative datasets do not exist; however, it is an infrastructure-deposited EU-OPENSCREEN project resource, not systematic retrospective mining of historical literature. It does not estimate publication omission or Janus-specific incremental coverage; submitter-defined calls and assay-specific detection limits still require context-aware interpretation.
column20: Relevance 3/3 to existing negative-resource prior art and data schema; Janus novelty must be tested as historical source-confirmed recovery plus exact incremental coverage, not dataset existence.

title: BioMiner: A Multi-modal System for Automated Mining of Protein-Ligand Bioactivity Data from Literature
research_question: Can multimodal protein-ligand bioactivity records be extracted at scale and improve downstream models?
negative_definition: protein-ligand bioactivity values; false negatives refer to omitted annotations recovered during benchmark verification, not biological negative outcomes; exact qualifier/censor representation in released records not yet audited
data_source: BioVista: 16,457 entries from 500 papers; application corpus: 82,262 records from 11,683 papers
method: multimodal document parsing plus structure recognition and human-in-the-loop verification
validation_or_evaluation: held-out BioVista test set; downstream pretraining, QSAR, and annotation applications
main_finding: Reports F1 0.323 for complete bioactivity triplets and downstream improvements from extracted data
limitation_or_gap: 2026 preprint and public README define/exemplify protein-ligand-value records; displayed schema has type/value/unit but no dedicated negative-state field. Drive-hosted full records were not inspected, so qualifier/negative coverage remains unresolved
relevance_to_janus: Critical novelty update: Janus must focus on negative-specific representation, provenance, and controlled incremental value rather than general bioactivity extraction

title: The Fragility of Bioactivity Prediction: Rigorous Dataset Splits Expose the Illusion of ML Accuracy
research_question: How does increasing train-test dissimilarity affect reported bioactivity prediction performance?
negative_definition: not a negative-data study
data_source: bioactivity prediction datasets under multiple splitting regimes
method: comparison of k-nearest-neighbor and modern ML models under increasingly strict splits
validation_or_evaluation: out-of-distribution evaluation across split regimes
main_finding: Reports comparable performance between simple similarity methods and complex models and sharp degradation as test compounds move out of distribution
limitation_or_gap: does not evaluate literature-derived negative evidence
relevance_to_janus: Supports strict structure-aware evaluation and a simple similarity baseline for any claimed Janus gain

title: zERExtractor: An Automated Platform for Enzyme-Catalyzed Reaction Data Extraction from Scientific Literature
research_question: Can enzyme kinetics and reaction data be extracted across text tables and molecular figures?
negative_definition: negative-state extraction is not an explicit reported target in the checked preprint/article text; absence from the task description is not proof the released data contain no negative records
data_source: 270 P450-related papers with over 1000 annotated tables and about 5000 biological fields
method: multimodal extraction with OCR, relation extraction, molecular diagram recognition, expert correction, and active learning
validation_or_evaluation: benchmark evaluation for table recognition, molecular images, and relation extraction
main_finding: Reports an expert-annotated enzyme literature extraction benchmark and structured capture of kinetic values, substrates, enzyme sequences, relative activities, and conditions
limitation_or_gap: Published in JCIM in 2026; broad enzymology extraction is established, while a typed negative-state task/ontology and its performance were not found in the checked report; released data coverage remains unaudited
relevance_to_janus: Directly narrows novelty: a Janus study must test negative-specific evidence recovery and value rather than general enzyme-data extraction

title: Rethinking Benchmarks and Models for Enzyme Specificity Prediction
domain: enzyme substrate and reaction prediction evaluation
research_question: Do current enzyme-substrate models generalize to unseen enzymes and substrates in discovery-like settings?
negative_definition: not a negative-data study; candidate pairs in the benchmark must not be assumed experimentally negative without evidence
data_source: published enzyme-screen datasets and a curated CYP reaction set with 2922 reactions across 768 enzymes
method: held-out enzyme/substrate evaluation and CYP ranking benchmark with supervised and structure-aware models
validation_or_evaluation: unseen enzyme and substrate tests plus ranking among candidate CYPs
main_finding: Reports that representative models can approach random performance on some held-out enzyme-substrate settings and often fail to beat BLAST in CYP ranking; structure-aware approach improves the task benchmark
limitation_or_gap: preprint; informs task design and OOD evaluation rather than negative-data extraction or independent utility of measured negatives
relevance_to_janus: Adjacent methodological evidence; use to set realistic task evaluation, not as evidence that negative evidence is missing

title: Machine learning modeling of family wide enzyme-substrate specificity screens
research_question: Can standardized literature-derived family-wide screens support models of enzyme-substrate compatibility?
negative_definition: measured enzyme-substrate pairs labeled active or inactive at thresholds from the original studies
data_source: six literature-derived enzyme-family screens covering about 1000 to 36000 pairs per family
method: curation of sequences and substrate SMILES plus CPI and single-task models
validation_or_evaluation: held-out enzyme discovery and substrate discovery tasks with standardized splits
main_finding: Curates and standardizes measured multi-enzyme multi-substrate screens and finds interaction models often fail to outperform single-task baselines
limitation_or_gap: All models use the measured binary labels, but the study does not ablate negative labels against matched-size alternatives; it demonstrates modeling with measured inactive outcomes, not an independent causal benefit from negatives. It does not recover diffuse prose/supplement negatives
relevance_to_janus: Direct prior art for extracting measured inactive outcomes from papers and modeling them; any novelty claim must go beyond dense-screen panel curation. Also a design template for consistent assay thresholds and extrapolation splits

title: A general model to predict small molecule substrates of enzymes based on machine and deep learning
research_question: Can a general model predict enzyme substrate scope from experimentally confirmed positives?
negative_definition: three similarity-matched putative negatives sampled per positive because systematic negative enzyme-small-molecule data were unavailable
data_source: 18,351 experimentally supported positive enzyme-substrate pairs plus generated negative pairs
method: protein and molecule representations with gradient boosted trees and graph neural networks
validation_or_evaluation: enzyme-level held-out test set; positive observations are experimentally supported, while negatives are sampled
main_finding: Reports strong substrate prediction performance using experimentally supported positives and sampled negative pairs
limitation_or_gap: Negative training and test labels are generated by the same sampling rule; high accuracy on this split does not validate the biological truth of each putative non-substrate. Authors note false negatives are possible and expected to be rare, but do not compare against an experimentally adjudicated negative test set or ablate matched real negatives
relevance_to_janus: Directly demonstrates the distinction between confirmed positives plus synthetic negatives and real tested negative evidence; supports a future evaluation design with an independently measured negative holdout

title: PubChem BioAssay database and data model
research_question: Can deposited assay outcomes and tested substances be queried and retrieved at scale?
negative_definition: depositor-provided assay activity outcomes commonly active or inactive plus assay-specific measurements
data_source: PubChem BioAssay records and associated assay descriptions and tested substances
method: database submission schema and searchable downloadable assay records with programmatic access
validation_or_evaluation: query by assay and outcome with assay-specific result data and provenance attributed to submitters
main_finding: Provides a large established infrastructure for structured screening outcomes including inactive records
limitation_or_gap: assay outcome labels are contributor-defined and assay-specific; database documentation does not establish systematic extraction of negative findings from full-text papers
relevance_to_janus: Important existing resource; Janus novelty must demonstrate incremental historical evidence recovery and added value beyond structured inactive screens

title: NegBioDB: A Negative-Results Database and Dual ML/LLM Benchmark for Biomedical Sciences
research_question: Can a multi-domain negative-data resource support conventional ML and LLM benchmarks?
negative_definition: domain-specific mixture of potency-threshold inactive labels trial-failure labels curated non-interactions gene-essentiality labels and variant labels; these are not one common evidence state
data_source: self-reported five-domain aggregation from 17 sources including ChEMBL PubChem BindingDB DAVIS AACT IntAct DepMap and ClinVar
method: data integration and domain-specific ML/LLM benchmarks with multiple split and negative-sampling controls
validation_or_evaluation: dataset-card-reported random and cold-start splits and model results; complete parent evaluation and independent reproduction not verified
main_finding: Public dataset card reports about 64M records across DTI clinical trial failure PPI gene essentiality and variant pathogenicity; DTI config defines inactive/active thresholds and excludes an intermediate pChEMBL band
limitation_or_gap: public repo/dataset card rather than verified peer-reviewed paper; PPI label sources include experimental/literature, model-predicted, low-score, and STRING zero-evidence categories; author companion says some parent corpus and per-pair predictions are held pending submission
relevance_to_janus: Major scope-overlap risk for a broad cross-domain resource proposal; audit labels and availability by evidence tier, do not equate database-derived thresholds with historical literature-text recovery

title: BioN∅T: A searchable database of biomedical negated sentences
domain: biomedical negation detection and literature retrieval
research_question: Can negated biomedical sentences be found with negation scope and local textual context?
negative_definition: sentences containing linguistic negation
data_source: about 32 million negated sentences extracted from over 336 million sentences in PubMed PMC and Elsevier text
method: NegScope negation-scope detection plus indexed sentence retrieval and neighboring-context display
validation_or_evaluation: case studies for gene-disease associations and manual review of returned sentences
main_finding: Demonstrates large-scale negated-sentence retrieval with scope and adjacent context
limitation_or_gap: does not explicitly normalize chemicals or assays or classify experimental claims as inactive below detection failed or untested; original paper names entity recognition and normalization as future work
relevance_to_janus: Direct prior art for general negation search and context retention; a molecular-data contribution must add entity and assay grounding plus typed experimental outcomes

title: Classifying Negative Findings in Biomedical Publications
research_question: Can a negated sentence be classified as reporting an actual negative research finding rather than merely containing negation?
negative_definition: sentence-level negative scientific findings distinguished from other sentences containing no or not
data_source: manually annotated and convenience-sampled biomedical abstract sentences
method: multinomial naive Bayes and SVM with bag-of-words part-of-speech shallow-parse and local cue features
validation_or_evaluation: five-fold cross-validation on a balanced dataset
main_finding: Reports best accuracy of 84% for identifying negative findings at sentence level
limitation_or_gap: small balanced abstract dataset; does not identify molecular assay entities or recover typed observation-level assay outcomes
relevance_to_janus: Establishes prior art beyond negation-scope detection; a project must add entity-assay grounding, experimental-state distinctions, provenance and context

title: LIT-PCBA: An Unbiased Data Set for Machine Learning and Virtual Screening
research_question: Can carefully filtered dose-response screening assays support less-biased virtual-screening and ML evaluation?
negative_definition: confirmed active/inactive compounds selected from dose-response PubChem bioassays with assay artifacts and property biases filtered
data_source: 149 PubChem dose-response bioassays initially processed; final benchmark reports 15 targets and 7844 actives; MAPK1 raw Full file has 308 actives/62,629 inactives while AVE T+V split has 308/61,567
method: curation of assay outcomes artifact filtering and asymmetric validation embedding (AVE)
validation_or_evaluation: virtual-screening evaluation with 2D fingerprint similarity 3D shape similarity and docking
main_finding: Provides direct precedent for molecule-level experimentally screened inactive records curated into a benchmark and used for model evaluation; official MAPK1 Full and AVE packages were directly inspected
limitation_or_gap: labels are assay-specific and dataset is a curated screening benchmark rather than historical full-text negative-result extraction; 1062 Full inactives are absent from AVE train+validation split, whereas 3449 AID 995 inactive observations plus active/inconclusive outcomes remain outside Full for unresolved reasons
relevance_to_janus: Strong baseline and competitor: any literature-recovery proposal must show assay-matched incremental coverage and controlled benefit beyond LIT-PCBA and existing PubChem outcomes

title: Assay-Aware BindingDB: Curating Experimental Context for Binding Affinity Prediction
domain: assay-context extraction and context-aware affinity prediction
research_question: Can assay metadata extracted from primary literature structure BindingDB affinity observations and improve binding-affinity prediction?
negative_definition: Quantitative protein-ligand Kd/Ki/IC50 observations across ITC, SPR, RBA and FPA; a likely companion public artifact retains censored < or > relations but excludes them from model-ready splits, without explicitly labeling them inactive
data_source: arXiv authors report 74,425 retained pairs from 5,991 papers; likely related anonymous HF artifact exposes 269,023 full rows across four assay types plus PMID-level train/validation/test seeds (authorship/version linkage not explicit)
method: Two-stage Qwen context extraction plus ontology-conditioned JSON; Qwen3 embedding combined with frozen Boltz-2 features; context-ablation and context-only comparisons on PMID-level splits
validation_or_evaluation: Paper reports extraction presence F1 >=0.947 and semantic accuracy >=0.913; 10 paper-level splits; combined-test MSE 1.27 to 1.19, Pearson r 0.64 to 0.67, c-index 0.73 to 0.74 (n=65,169)
main_finding: Context improves aggregate author-reported affinity metrics modestly, but gains vary by assay; ITC MSE worsens and RBA MSE gain is not significant
limitation_or_gap: arXiv v1 preprint; matching HF artifact is public but uploader anonymous and not linked in paper; no code or license was found; HF full row count 269,023 differs from paper's 113,311 candidates/74,425 retained; censored measurements omitted from model-ready splits
relevance_to_janus: Very high-overlap competitor: literature context plus source passages plus model benefit already exists, and censored affinity records are publicly retained. A distinct contribution must focus on typed explicit inactive/no-effect evidence, assay-aware interpretation of censored bounds, incremental recovery, and negative-specific modeling/evaluation

title: Enhancing uncertainty quantification in drug discovery with censored regression labels
domain: QSAR and uncertainty quantification with censored labels
research_question: Can molecular property models use left/right-censored experimental labels to improve prediction and uncertainty estimates?
negative_definition: threshold-only partial quantitative measurements (e.g. values above/below assay/reporting limits)
data_source: 15 internal pharmaceutical assays spanning target IC50/EC50 and ADME-T; censoring ranges from 0% to 63%; core row-level data are proprietary
method: Tobit censored likelihood for Gaussian models and one-sided loss for ensembles/MC-dropout/Bayesian models; temporal splits and with/without-censored-label ablation
validation_or_evaluation: author-reported temporal evaluation and NLL ablation; inclusion usually improved or matched epistemic uncertainty for ensembles/Bayesian models; aleatoric gains concentrated more in assays with >35% censored records
main_finding: Strong direct evidence that censored quantitative observations can improve uncertainty modeling; publicly released UQ4DD code includes TDC examples but cannot reproduce proprietary paper results
limitation_or_gap: Censored measurements are not equivalent to explicitly reported inactive/no-effect findings; main ablation emphasizes uncertainty NLL rather than negative-class prediction; internal data unavailable for independent reproduction
relevance_to_janus: High relevance as a model-value precedent and strong baseline; narrows novelty toward reliable extraction/assay grounding of explicit negative evidence, incremental coverage, and negative-specific benefits beyond censored regression

title: QSAR Analysis Involving Assay Results Which are only Known to be Greater Than, or Less Than Some Cut-off Limit
research_question: Can regression use assay values known only to lie above or below a cutoff?
negative_definition: left/right-censored property or activity values rather than exact measurements
data_source: Free-Wilson R-group activity-score calculations with assay values censored at measurement limits
method: imputation-based regression method for estimating latent values underlying censored observations
validation_or_evaluation: method stability and accuracy evaluated in Free-Wilson activity-score setting
main_finding: Early molecular-QSAR precedent demonstrating that threshold-censored values carry usable information and need not be discarded
limitation_or_gap: narrow method/application; does not mine literature or distinguish explicit experimental inactive statements from censoring
relevance_to_janus: Relevant historical method precedent; rules out claiming that learning from censored molecular assay values is itself novel

title: ChEMBL Activity schema and PubChem integration documentation
domain: structured bioactivity data curation and semantics
research_question: How are quantitative measurements, censored relations, categorical outcomes and interpretations represented in ChEMBL?
negative_definition: numeric relation-bounded outcomes plus text outcomes and comments; PubChem summaries may be stored in activity comments
data_source: ChEMBL activity and assay data model; official depositor guide and interface FAQ on PubChem integration
method: Separate VALUE, RELATION, TEXT_VALUE and ACTIVITY_COMMENT fields; pChEMBL calculation requires standard_relation='='; import guidance and provenance/interpretation notes
validation_or_evaluation: Schema documentation and stated integration behavior; no new empirical coverage or model evaluation performed here
main_finding: Official schema distinguishes quantitative censoring from categorical text outcomes and supports preserving an interpretation/threshold alongside numerical activity; ChEMBL documents that censored relation records are not eligible for pChEMBL
limitation_or_gap: Documentation specifies allowed representation, not prevalence, record-level fidelity or completeness of source-paper context; PubChem integration focuses on AC result types and is not proof every binary summary is imported; the prevalence and benchmark impact of pChEMBL exclusion are not yet measured
relevance_to_janus: Directly informs the schema and data-source audit; weakens claims that structured databases lack typed negative labels, while leaving coverage and recoverability open

title: Large-scale comparison of machine learning methods for drug target prediction on ChEMBL
domain: large-scale molecular bioactivity benchmark and target prediction
research_question: Can standardized machine learning methods predict compound-target activity across many ChEMBL assays?
negative_definition: explicit ChEMBL activity comments (Active/inactive/Not Active including single-concentration no-response comment) plus threshold-assigned labels derived from values and censored relations
data_source: ChEMBL 20; final benchmark of 1,310 assays and 4,743,712 assay measurements across 456,331 compounds
method: curated labels from standard activity_comment values and potency thresholds conditioned on units/standard_relation; conflicting labels removed; benchmark comparison of nine prediction methods
validation_or_evaluation: nested chemical-cluster cross-validation; authors report deep learning methods outperforming competing methods and benchmark performance comparable in many cases to in-vitro tests
main_finding: Direct prior art: explicit Not Active comments and censored numerical observations were converted into active/inactive benchmark labels and used at million-record scale
limitation_or_gap: Database-derived labels and thresholds, not novel full-text mining; no incremental recovery beyond ChEMBL; no type-separated ablation or same-data no-negative-label comparison, so the study does not establish an independent causal effect of measured negatives
relevance_to_janus: Very high relevance: rules out claiming first use of structured inactive/censored bioactivity labels for molecular ML; leaves a narrower gap in recovering and validating novel non-duplicate evidence beyond current databases, with provenance and type-specific benefit

title: Data Leakage and Redundancy in the LIT-PCBA Benchmark
domain: molecular virtual-screening benchmark integrity and stereochemistry-aware split audit
research_question: Do identity/analog overlap and simple similarity baselines undermine LIT-PCBA model-generalization claims?
negative_definition: Experimental active/inactive assay labels in LIT-PCBA, examined for stereo-agnostic 2D identity overlap and analog similarity
data_source: LIT-PCBA train/query/validation sets across targets; audit paper reports 2,491 stereo-agnostic inactive overlaps and 323 ALDH1 active analog pairs at ECFP4 Tanimoto >=0.6
method: RDKit Morgan/ECFP4 similarity baseline and overlap analysis; audit notebook uses a chirality-insensitive fingerprint by default
validation_or_evaluation: Authors report median raw EF1%=4.15 for a parameter-free similarity baseline; this turn did not independently reproduce the split statistics or scores
main_finding: Directly warns that split composition and molecular representation may confound apparent value of experimentally measured negative labels in screening benchmarks
limitation_or_gap: A technical counterreview reports exact isomeric identity overlap vanishes when stereochemistry is retained; the same stereoforms may remain indistinguishable to achiral 2D models. Audit split archives currently return 404, preventing independent replication. Preprint and counterreview are not a settled consensus; raw EF is class-size sensitive
relevance_to_janus: High relevance to evaluating negative-data model value and preserving assay-specific labels, but does not establish that negative data are absent, harmful, or newly recoverable; use as a design warning and stratify stereo-blind/stereo-aware, exact/analog overlap and split regimes

title: How to Achieve Better Results Using PASS-Based Virtual Screening: Case Study for Kinase Inhibitors
domain: kinase inhibitor QSAR and target-specific versus cross-target training labels
research_question: Does a model benefit from target-specific experimentally measured active/inactive data versus merged cross-target data that treats untested compounds as conditionally inactive?
negative_definition: Target-specific measured active/inactive at a 1 uM or 50% inhibition rule; 'conditionally inactive' means no activity record for that target, not experimentally confirmed inactive
data_source: ChEMBL 20 training data: 152 human kinases, 173,275 activity points (62,309 active and 110,966 inactive) across 55,162 compounds; ChEMBL 23 external compound-target pairs
method: PASS/MNA models trained as target-specific measured I-sets, merged actives plus true and conditional inactives (MAI), or merged actives only (MA); stratified five-fold and ChEMBL23 external validation with resampled BEDROC
validation_or_evaluation: Authors report target-specific I-sets generally outperform MAI/MA in classification and early recognition; 13 kinases favor MA/MAI in early recognition; AUC/balanced accuracy less sensitive to class ratio than precision/F1
main_finding: Direct evidence that untested-as-negative cross-target labels can reduce performance relative to target-specific measured labels, with target-dependent exceptions; not a same-target ablation isolating the causal benefit of adding measured negatives
limitation_or_gap: Specialized PASS/MNA pipeline; training schemes differ in target aggregation and label semantics; measured I-set advantage does not prove all measured negatives improve all molecular models; external ChEMBL version split is not prospective experimental validation
relevance_to_janus: Very high relevance: strengthens the case that measured assay-specific labels should not be replaced by assumed negatives and that negative-label utility is target-dependent; still leaves the incremental value of adding source-verified measured negatives under matched data size, class ratio and test split unresolved

title: Inactive-enriched machine-learning models exploiting patent data improve structure-based virtual screening for PDL1 dimerizers
domain: PD-L1 structure-based virtual screening and inactive-enriched scoring functions
research_question: Do experimentally measured inactive compounds, generated property-matched decoys, or random decoys improve docking-based scoring compared with actives-only training?
negative_definition: PubChem BioAssay AID 2316 assay true inactives; DeepCoy-generated property-matched decoys; ZINC random property-unmatched decoys; active-only potency split for classification baseline
data_source: PD-L1 patent actives; AID 2316 screened 28,781 compounds with one active; docked test set includes 297 actives plus 18,550 true-inactive instances; training uses 371 actives and different negative-source/size options
method: Docking-based PLEC/GRID features; 10 supervised algorithms in classification and regression; train/test partitions compare TrueInactives, DeepCoy, RandomDecoys, ActivesOnly; separate true-inactive and DeepCoy test sets
main_finding: Inactive-enriched models strongly outperform active-only in this PD-L1 SBVS case; within inactive-enriched settings, true-inactive training did not significantly outperform much larger random-decoy training, while using 23x more random decoys improved performance on true-inactive test
limitation_or_gap: Direct but highly task-specific value evidence; negative counts and total training sizes vary substantially; active-only classification changes task to high/low potency; benefits cannot be causally assigned to measured-negative status apart from sample size, docking representation, target and sampling
relevance_to_janus: Directly relevant to negative-data utility and source comparisons, but limited to one target and docking-based structure scoring; supports a narrow experimental design separating label provenance from quantity and task representation, not a general claim for ligand-only bioactivity prediction

title: A preclinical secondary pharmacology resource illuminates target-adverse drug reaction associations of marketed drugs
domain: Preclinical secondary pharmacology / marketed-drug target profiling
research_question: Are assay-level activity and inactivity results represented in existing public and subscription bioactivity resources, and does coverage differ by result type?
negative_definition: SPD concentration-response summaries; AC50 thresholds distinguish high activity (<1 μM), lower activity/inactive comparisons (≥10 μM); threshold/censored results must remain distinct from qualitative binary inactive labels
data_source: 1,958 drugs tested against 200 assays; 147,653 curves summarized as 121,097 drug-assay pairs; cross-referenced against ChEMBL, DrugCentral, and subscription sources
method: Cross-resource overlap and activity-strength comparisons, including matched SPD/ChEMBL pairs
main_finding: Authors report ~95% of results unique to SPD and ~36% of AC50<1 μM results unique; among matched results, 66% of SPD AC50≥10 μM records have ChEMBL median AC50<10 μM, while 82% of SPD AC50<0.1 μM records show similar potency in ChEMBL
limitation_or_gap: SPD-unique does not mean never published; authors note some results can be found by manual literature search. Assay composition and protocol differences can explain part of discrepancy. Local recomputation using an approximate field-based rule gives 94.81% overall unique and 37.60% active unique, not an exact replication; no literature-negative extraction benchmark or controlled ML benefit test
relevance_to_janus: Directly supports undercoverage of inactive results in commonly used sources and motivates distinguishing resource coverage from publication bias; a systematic panel resource rather than retrospective full-text mining, so does not complete Janus's extraction or model-utility aims

title: Predicting novel substrates for enzymes with minimal experimental effort with active learning
research_question: Can literature-sourced measured inactive compounds plus strategically selected experiments support enzyme-substrate classification?
negative_definition: Known substrates are positive observations; tested inactive compounds manually recovered from primary papers are measured negatives; untested and random candidates are not equivalent
data_source: BRENDA and primary literature plus datasets for MenD, carboxylic acid reductase, amino-acid ester hydrolase and HAPMO; manual negative literature search
method: SVMs with cheminformatics fingerprints and active-learning prioritization; eight purchased compounds assayed for MenD
validation_or_evaluation: Cross-validation learning curves; experimental assay of selected MenD candidates; three model-new MenD candidates also tested
main_finding: Demonstrates feasibility of manually finding tested inactive substrate pairs missing from BRENDA and using them in models; active learning selected informative follow-up experiments
limitation_or_gap: Small enzyme-specific studies and limited chemical space; no prospective evaluation of a general extraction system; paper does not isolate causal gain from adding only literature-recovered negatives
relevance_to_janus: Very high relevance to biochemical feasibility: direct precedent for literature recovery of assay-tested negatives beyond a curated resource and for model use; narrows novelty to scalable, typed, provenance-preserving extraction and controlled incremental value

title: Robots and Minimal, Physics-Informed Features: A Hybrid Framework for Enzyme Catalysis
domain: robotic enzyme-substrate screening and OOD activity prediction
research_question: Can standardized experimental active/inactive substrate screens and physics-informed features improve enzyme-substrate prediction across enzyme families?
negative_definition: Measured endpoint yields thresholded as active if >1% and inactive if ≤1% under specified assay conditions; the threshold defines operational inactivity, not universal non-substrate status
data_source: Robotic experiments on 374 enzyme-substrate pairs across yADH, hlADH, TA-At and TA-Af, each measured in triplicate; external FDC, phosphatase and esterase datasets
method: Random-forest and other ML models using docking pose/orientation and quantum-chemical features; enzyme-family held-out train/validation/test evaluation
validation_or_evaluation: Five-fold CV, family-held-out OOD evaluation and external literature datasets; authors report mean test balanced accuracy 0.67 and better OOD performance than descriptor-heavy baselines
main_finding: Shows that standardized real measured inactive outcomes plus chemically diverse substrate panels can support cross-family prediction; provides public raw yields, structures and code
limitation_or_gap: Prospective robotic data generation, not historical literature mining; only four enzyme systems in new data; the ≤1% cutoff operationalizes inactivity and is chosen partly for reliable measurement and class balance; no test of whether recovering old literature negatives adds coverage beyond the new screen
relevance_to_janus: Very high relevance to model-utility evidence and competitive landscape: rules out novelty of merely building an enzyme active/inactive dataset and demonstrating OOD prediction; does not address scalable recovery of previously published negative observations, provenance/context extraction or incremental coverage from literature

title: Exploring bacterial carboxylate reductases for the reduction of bifunctional carboxylic acids
research_question: Can a common biochemical screen map measured CAR activity and low/no-detect outcomes across a broad substrate panel?
negative_definition: Assay-relative activity/no-detect outcome in a purified-enzyme NADPH-oxidation screen; do not equate an inactive CAR preparation with a substrate-level negative
data_source: 15 purified CAR proteins screened against 87 carboxylic-acid substrates; detailed Table S3 and Figures S3-S4 are supplementary
method: NADPH-oxidation assay with common buffer/cofactor/substrate conditions; product/bioconversion assays used for selected candidates
validation_or_evaluation: Screened panel reported activity spectra; no ML utility test; article indicates no detectable activity for selected substrate classes
main_finding: A dense assay-context-rich negative/low-activity panel is a candidate extraction-schema benchmark and distinguishes tested no-detect from untested; the paper reports a CAR preparation inactive toward benzoate, which is a different label type
limitation_or_gap: Prospective complete screening, not historical literature mining or publication-bias analysis; SI matrix was not inspected because download verification/403 blocked access; no row-level counts or newly extracted records asserted
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 2/3: directly informs assay context and typed label schema, but only adjacent evidence for recovering fragmented historical negatives

title: Phylogenomically Guided Identification of Industrially Relevant GH1 β-Glucosidases through DNA Synthesis and Nanostructure-Initiator Mass Spectrometry
domain: GH1 enzyme substrate specificity and high-throughput activity screening
research_question: Can high-throughput measured enzyme–substrate observations distinguish tested non-detection from missing data and technical failure?
negative_definition: No detectable turnover for defined substrate probes under specified NIMS/HPLC conditions; separate from unexpressed enzyme, untested pair, or universal inactive claim
data_source: 175 synthesized GH1 proteins and 10,080 assay data points across multiplexed substrate/temperature/pH combinations; selected observations validated by HPLC
method: NIMS conversion readout with triplicate reactions and nonenzymatic background correction; selected enzyme/substrate conditions assessed by HPLC
validation_or_evaluation: Authors report nine expressed enzymes with no NIMS-substrate activity and no detectable HPLC activity against tested natural substrates for the follow-up nine; no ML negative-data ablation
main_finding: Provides a large measured-screen precedent and concrete distinctions among no-detect, assay modality, tested context, and expression failure
limitation_or_gap: Prospective high-throughput screen, not retrospective literature mining or publication-bias analysis; n=10,080 is total points, not negatives; no controlled test of ML benefit from negative observations
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 2/3: useful for a biochemical label/context schema and benchmark selection, but not direct evidence for historical recovery or model utility

title: TemBERTure: advancing protein thermostability prediction with deep learning and attention mechanisms
research_question: Can protein sequence models predict thermal class/Tm, and what are limitations of organism-derived proxy labels?
negative_definition: Thermophilic versus non-thermophilic classes assigned largely from organism growth temperature (>60°C versus <30°C); these are proxy labels, not per-protein substrate-activity negatives
data_source: TemBERTureDB combines Meltome Atlas-derived proteins, UniProt proteomes, and BacDive/NCBI organism-linked sequences; balanced to about 300,000 sequences per class
method: Protein language-model classifier and Tm regressor with adapter fine-tuning; sequence-cluster-aware splits and external tests
validation_or_evaluation: Authors report classifier performance and explicitly note thermostable proteins in non-thermophilic proteomes and possible species-origin signal in Tm predictions
main_finding: Large-scale precedent for task-specific negative/proxy labels; highlights that model labels and biological assay observations must not be conflated
limitation_or_gap: Does not recover measured enzyme–substrate negatives from literature and cannot establish model utility of activity-negative evidence; organism growth-temperature proxy may mislabel individual proteins
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to negative-label ontology and evaluation risk, but 0 direct evidence for measured biochemical negative utility

title: A Machine Learning Approach for the Prediction of Thermostable β-Glucosidases
research_question: Can graph-based structural signatures classify GH1 beta-glucosidases associated with thermophilic organisms?
negative_definition: Positive/negative class is organism-level thermal proxy: UniProt organism names containing 'therm' versus sampled names without it ('likely non-thermophilic'); not measured enzyme inactivity
data_source: UniProt EC 3.2.1.21 sequence set; 3,000 initial sequences sampled by organism-name heuristic; 1,717 structures retained after filtering and structure retrieval
method: Graph-based structural signatures with seven classifiers; random train/test split after class balancing
validation_or_evaluation: Reports 81.6% CatBoost test accuracy; no activity-negative recovery or negative-data ablation
main_finding: Direct GH1/ML example illustrating that a paper's 'negative' can mean absence of a taxonomy string rather than observed biochemical inactivity
limitation_or_gap: Heuristic proxy labels may encode taxonomy and do not establish per-protein thermostability or substrate-specific assay outcomes; paper does not address literature extraction
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 2/3: useful adjacent prior art and label-semantics caution, not evidence for the main measured-negative retrieval or utility claim

title: A novel benchmark dataset for enzyme function prediction reveals the limitations of state-of-the-art models
domain: Enzyme function prediction benchmark with structure-guided non-functional decoys
research_question: Can EC predictors distinguish catalytically disrupted variants from their functional parent enzymes?
negative_definition: Putative non-functional decoy sequences generated in silico by mutating annotated catalytic residues or surrounding active-site shells; not measured enzyme-substrate inactive pairs
data_source: Swiss-Prot/UniProt reviewed sequences with full EC, Rhea ID, and length filters; subset with annotated active sites used to generate catalytic and 5/10/15 Å decoys
method: Benchmarks DIAMOND, CLEAN, and DeepEC against parent EC labels across perturbation radii
validation_or_evaluation: Preprint reports >90% original-EC false positive rates for DIAMOND/CLEAN on low perturbations; DeepEC is more sensitive to larger perturbations but still misses subtle catalytic-site changes
main_finding: Direct and timely prior art for negative-like examples in enzyme model evaluation; highlights homology/phylogeny shortcuts and supports challenging negative benchmarks
limitation_or_gap: Preprint, not peer reviewed at audit date; computational decoys are not experimental negatives; cross-model comparison cannot isolate causal benefit of negative training; no literature-mining/provenance/context extraction or matched ablation
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to model evaluation and novelty boundary, distinct from retrospective recovery of measured negatives

title: Enzyme promiscuity prediction using hierarchy-informed multi-label classification
domain: Enzyme-substrate promiscuity prediction with inhibitor supervision
research_question: Does supervising known enzyme inhibitors as hard negatives improve molecule ranking compared with treating those same observations as unlabeled?
negative_definition: BRENDA-reported enzyme inhibitors are known inhibitory interactions and hard negatives to substrate compatibility; not equivalent to substrate pairs experimentally tested and found inactive
data_source: BRENDA substrate-positive and inhibitor interactions across 983 EC numbers; 25,872 positive pairings and 13,087 inhibitor pairings
method: Hierarchical multi-label models including EPP-HMCNF; compares inhibitor-informed supervision with inhibitor examples left unlabeled under similarity weighting
validation_or_evaluation: Random and realistic molecular splits; inhibitor and unlabeled test sets; reports EPP-HMCNF realistic-split reduced-set AUROC 0.849→0.857, AP 0.131→0.149, R-PREC 0.111→0.126 after inhibitor supervision
main_finding: Direct evidence that known measured inhibitor labels can improve enzyme-molecule prediction beyond leaving the same records unlabeled; includes a useful label-supervision ablation
limitation_or_gap: Inhibitors are not tested non-substrates; improvement is model/task-specific; results not independently rerun and do not test historical literature-recovered no-detect observations
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to the broad utility of measured negative-like evidence; 2/3 to retrospective recovery of assay-specific inactive substrate pairs

title: SABIO-RK: an updated resource for manually curated biochemical reaction kinetics
research_question: Can reaction-oriented, literature-curated kinetic records provide a second database comparator for exact assay-level negative-observation recovery?
negative_definition: No dedicated negative category established in this audit; SABIO-RK entries represent reactions/kinetics and should not be read as complete tested-pair matrices
data_source: SABIO-RK literature-curated and submitted reaction kinetics; live query on 2026-09-30 found 2 xylobiose, 31 cellobiose, and 88 lactose substrate entries; 16 entries for EC 3.2.1.86
method: Live exact-UniProt/EC/substrate/source queries through the current SABIO-RK search API; inspected returned protein IDs, substrates, organisms, and PubMed references
validation_or_evaluation: Bounded database-coverage audit against 100-row GH1 NIMS pilot; exact IDs D4LC32, A0ACM7, Q55000, D4MF92 and Heins DOI/accession queries returned zero; substrate queries returned cross-organism positive kinetics records
main_finding: SABIO-RK is a comparator for structured positive reaction/kinetic evidence; its documented experimental-condition fields could support later comparison, but this pass did not establish condition-level matches. Exact record matching requires protein, substrate, and provenance rather than shared EC or substrate alone
limitation_or_gap: Zero query results do not prove absence from all fields/source literature; no observation-level measured-negative match or full database completeness estimate established
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to cross-resource coverage methodology; 2/3 to the core negative-evidence gap

title: Characterization of β-glucosidase activity of a Lactiplantibacillus plantarum 6-phospho-β-glucosidase
research_question: How are measured no-detect outcomes represented across structured activity tables, prose, and TLC figures, and how much assay context can be recovered?
negative_definition: Substrate-scoped: zero relative activity/no activity detected for two pNP glycosides; no hydrolysis of arbutin and cellobiose through 96 h. Not an enzyme-global inactive label
data_source: LpBgl5 from L. plantarum NCIM 2903; gene accession PQ462659; Table 1 relative activity panel and Figure 3 TLC time-course
method: Purified recombinant protein; standard pNP assay plus natural-glycoside TLC panel; positive almond β-glucosidase and empty-vector E. coli controls; triplicates
validation_or_evaluation: For pNP substrates: 10 mM substrate, 25 µg enzyme, pH 6, 40°C, 1 h, A405; for natural glycosides: 1 mM, 50 µg enzyme, pH 6, 40°C, TLC through 96 h
main_finding: Demonstrates that one paper can contain structured zero values and prose/figure-based no-hydrolysis records with substantially recoverable conditions; active substrates within the same panel prevent enzyme-level overgeneralization
limitation_or_gap: No analytical detection limit for zero/no-hydrolysis; TLC data are qualitative; original replicate/raw data not publicly available (data on reasonable request); convenience example only, no extraction benchmark or model-utility experiment; exact BRENDA sequence crosswalk attempted but unreturned; accession-based coverage remains unresolved
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to negative-observation extraction and context schema; no direct model-utility evidence

title: Loss of a conserved salt bridge in bacterial glycosyl hydrolase BglM-G1 improves substrate binding in temperate environments
domain: GH1 substrate specificity with table/prose label ambiguity
research_question: Can prose-level no-detect statements disambiguate table dashes without propagating a result from wild type to a variant?
negative_definition: Results paragraph in the BglM-G1 subsection states no activity was detected against tested alpha-glycosidic substrates, mapping to BglM-G1's two Table 1 alpha-substrate cells as qualitative panel-level negatives. The two H75R cells remain ambiguous dashes; the prose does not explicitly assign the result to H75R.
data_source: Synthetic BglM-G1 derived from GOS sequence and H75R variant; article notes a 99%-identity GenBank homolog KRO51423, not automatically the exact tested construct
method: Purified recombinant enzymes; aryl-glycoside specificity assay; substrate blanks; at least three technical replicates
validation_or_evaluation: 2 mM substrate, 50 mM sodium citrate pH 6.0, 45°C, spectrophotometric p-nitrophenol; enzyme amount stated as a range 2.0–207.0 pmol, not resolved per cell
main_finding: Useful difficult extraction/annotation case: paragraph location and subsection subject permit class-level evidence to support two wild-type substrate observations, while two H75R dashes remain unresolved; exposes both under-calling and over-propagation risks.
limitation_or_gap: Table dash semantics remain undefined; exact per-cell enzyme amount, detection limit, timepoint detail and raw replicates unavailable. No H75R-specific source outcome or database crosswalk established; no model-utility test.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to evidence granularity, entity resolution and negative-label extraction; no direct model-utility evidence

title: Negative Example Selection for Protein Function Prediction: The NoGO Database
domain: Protein-function prediction and inferred negative-example selection
research_question: Can high-quality inferred negatives outperform random or heuristic negatives and improve downstream protein-function prediction?
negative_definition: Predicted negatives inferred from absence/co-occurrence patterns in GO annotations under a positive-unlabeled/open-world setting; not experimentally tested enzyme-substrate inactive outcomes
data_source: Archived and current Gene Ontology annotations across human, mouse, yeast, worm, rice, and Arabidopsis; ranked predicted negatives released through NoGO
method: SNOB, NETL, Rocchio and comparator heuristics/PU algorithms; temporal holdout to estimate newly positive annotations among predicted negatives
validation_or_evaluation: Measures false-negative predictions against future GO annotations; compares downstream GO function prediction AUROC when using selected vs random negatives
main_finding: Authors report fewer incorrect inferred negatives than several baselines and better downstream function-prediction performance using selected negatives; Arabidopsis case uses 313,592 predicted negatives
limitation_or_gap: GO non-annotation is not an assay negative and future GO annotations incompletely reveal false negatives; supports the general value of negative-label quality, not measured molecular activity negatives or literature mining
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 2/3: strong adjacent evidence that negative-example quality affects protein ML, but labels are inferred from annotation structure rather than experimental assay outcomes

title: The sugar donor specificity of plant family 1 glycosyltransferases (supplementary UGT donor dataset)
domain: Plant UGT donor-specificity; literature-curated enzyme-substrate outcomes
research_question: Can published plant GT1/UGT donor-specificity studies be consolidated into a sequence- and structure-linked reaction activity resource?
negative_definition: Binary activity labels: active if any conflicting source reports activity; reported measurements below 5% of the enzyme's strongest donor-acceptor reaction are classified inactive; CSV does not expose a distinct untested state
data_source: Zenodo supplementary compilation with 1,189 enzyme-donor-acceptor rows linked to literature DOIs; 218 enzyme labels, 10 donors, 110 acceptor strings in CSV
method: Manual aggregation of published UGT reaction results; conflict resolution favors positive; downloadable long-form CSV links enzyme accession/sequence, donor, acceptor SMILES and source DOI
validation_or_evaluation: Resource-level curation counts and review synthesis; no extraction benchmark, held-out prediction evaluation or negative-specific model ablation identified
main_finding: Demonstrates prior art for a focused literature-derived UGT specificity compilation with 590 binary inactive rows and per-row DOI fields
limitation_or_gap: The DOI is to a 2024 review with supplementary curated data, not a standalone extraction-method paper. Binary zero mixes literature-reported/threshold-derived outcomes; raw numeric activity, per-observation assay conditions, detection limits and a dedicated untested state are absent in the CSV. Seven reaction keys repeat without contradictory labels. Zenodo says 108 acceptors whereas CSV has 110 raw names pending identity normalization.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to narrow-domain literature curation and label provenance, 2/3 to recovery feasibility, 0/3 direct evidence of independent ML gains from negatives

title: Functional and informatics analysis enables glycosyltransferase activity prediction
domain: Plant GT1 family activity screening and ML prediction
research_question: Can enzyme sequence information and family-wide screening data predict glycosyltransferase activity with diverse acceptors/donors?
negative_definition: Green/amber/red screen outcomes are defined by signal-to-noise (>10, 1-10, <1); source repository encodes low/red class as binary inactive and omits source value 0 described as untested
data_source: Family-wide GT1 screening data in primary article and supplements; includes a 49-enzyme by six-donor Kaempferol panel with 278 compiled reaction rows in the later Zenodo dataset
method: Experimental GAR screening, sequence/family feature analysis, and GT-Predict machine-learning predictions; linked supplement displays assay outcomes and thresholds
validation_or_evaluation: Prediction performance against experimental glycosyltransferase screens; high-throughput GAR outcomes in the figure are single measurements
main_finding: Shows that dense experimental GT1 specificity screens and ML prediction already exist; its later curated UGT compilation uses 278 rows from this paper as a major cited source
limitation_or_gap: High-throughput cells are single measurements, so repeatability cannot be estimated; the later aggregate data discard raw S/N and full context, and do not conduct a negative-specific matched ablation. The source-level aggregate-label-to-pixel crosswalk remains incomplete.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to measured enzyme-substrate negatives already used in ML and evidence traceability; 0/3 to independently isolating negative-label benefit

title: Genome-wide identification and functional characterization of UDP-glucosyltransferase genes involved in flavonoid biosynthesis in Glycine max
research_question: What substrate and donor specificities do six recombinant soybean UGTs show across flavonoid acceptors?
negative_definition: Explicit table-level not-detectable cells are donor-specific (e.g. UGT88A13/quercetin: UDP-glucose positive, UDP-galactose not detected); the table defines dash as no detectable product
data_source: Primary article Table 1 and assay methods; also included in the Zenodo UGT compilation as 69 DOI-linked reaction rows (31 inactive, 38 active)
method: Expression and in-vitro assays of recombinant UGTs across flavonoid acceptors and UDP-glucose/UDP-galactose/UDP-glucuronic acid donors; product identification by HPLC/LC-MS
validation_or_evaluation: Table-level product detection outcomes, substrate-specificity and kinetic analyses; no reported independent validation of the supplementary binary compilation
main_finding: Provides a precise source-linked inactive example and specified assay context; shows how one paper's donor-specific table can anchor a binary inactive row
limitation_or_gap: One exact row was audited, not all 31 zeros. Enzyme-screen replicate count and detection limit were not stated in the checked methods. Abstract/discussion conflict with Results/Table 1 regarding UGT88A13 activity toward kaempferol/quercetin, so contradictions must remain explicit rather than be resolved from a single text span.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to assay-negative provenance and context; 2/3 to literature-recovery feasibility; 0/3 to independent ML benefit

title: Analysis of Two New Arabinosyltransferases Belonging to the Carbohydrate-Active Enzyme (CAZY) Glycosyl Transferase Family 1 Provides Insights into Disease Resistance and Sugar Donor Specificity
domain: Plant GT1/UGT donor-specificity assays for oat and soybean triterpene glycosyltransferases
research_question: Can biochemical assays identify plant GT1 sugar-donor specificity and residues controlling arabinosyltransferase activity?
negative_definition: Donor-specific nondetect: AsAAT1 with TCP has no detectable product for UDP-Glc and UDP-Gal but activity for UDP-Ara; Figure 3A reports three biological replicates and SD
data_source: Primary article and Figure 3A; represented by 32 DOI-linked rows in the later Zenodo UGT compilation (20 binary inactive, 12 active)
method: Recombinant UGT screening with UDP-Glc, UDP-Gal and UDP-Ara using 2,4,5-trichlorophenol as universal acceptor; follow-up natural acceptor assays and mutagenesis
validation_or_evaluation: Figure 3A spectrophotometric TCP-glycoside readout at 405 nm with n=3 biological replicates; later aggregate table does not provide matched raw values or separate test-level evaluation
main_finding: Two exact AsAAT1/TCP negative rows can be traced to explicit source prose; source retains replication metadata absent from the binary CSV, demonstrating why the evidence record should preserve donor, acceptor, readout and n
limitation_or_gap: Only two of 20 DOI-level aggregate zeros were individually mapped in this pass; no LOD/threshold was found for this screen in the checked source passage, and complete context/raw values are not retained in the aggregate. No negative-specific model ablation or independent ML benefit is tested.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to source-level negative provenance and context preservation; 2/3 to extraction feasibility; 0/3 direct ML utility

title: Characterization of Two Key Flavonoid 3-O-Glycosyltransferases Involved in the Formation of Flower Color in Rhododendron Delavayi
domain: Plant flavonoid 3-O-glycosyltransferase donor and acceptor specificity
research_question: How do Rd3GT1 and Rd3GT6 transfer different UDP-sugars across anthocyanidin acceptors, and what supports negative calls?
negative_definition: All 20 DOI-group binary zeros match Supplementary Tables S5/S6 entries marked ND (not detected due to low activity); the source reports three independent determinations
data_source: Primary article and official Supplementary Tables S5/S6; 33 DOI-linked rows in the Zenodo UGT compilation (20 zero, 13 one), representing 33 of 48 cells in the source's full 2-enzyme × 4-donor × 6-acceptor panel
method: In-vitro recombinant enzyme assays across anthocyanidin acceptors and UDP-sugar donors, with HPLC product analysis and supplemental relative-activity tables
validation_or_evaluation: Supplementary tables contain relative activity and means from three independent determinations; compilation reduces source rows to binary labels and does not test downstream ML utility
main_finding: All 20 compiled zero labels can be audited to source-table low-activity nondetects; Supplementary Table S6 resolves the apparent UDP-Ara/delphinidin prose ambiguity (UDP-Rha active; UDP-Ara ND)
limitation_or_gap: Fifteen cells from the full six-acceptor source grid are absent from the DOI group and cannot be imputed as inactive. Binary compilation loses numeric activities and replicate values; no negative-specific model ablation or independent ML benefit is tested.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to label provenance/context and missingness; 2/3 to source recovery; 0/3 direct ML utility

title: Functional Characterization of a Flavonoid Glycosyltransferase in Sweet Orange (Citrus sinensis)
domain: Sweet orange CsUGT76F1 flavonoid donor/acceptor specificity
research_question: Which flavonoid acceptors and UDP-sugar donors does recombinant CsUGT76F1 glycosylate, and what assay context supports the inactive calls?
negative_definition: Thirteen compiled zeros correspond to tested donor/acceptor combinations outside the reported UDP-Rha substrate scope; source explicitly says Rha does not glycosylate hesperetin, naringenin, or diosmetin and only Rha (among alternative donors) is accepted
data_source: Primary Frontiers article and its Results/Methods; represented by 20 DOI-linked Zenodo rows (13 zero, 7 one) across five acceptors and four donors
method: Recombinant CsUGT76F1 substrate-specificity assays with UDP-Glc, UDP-Gal, UDP-Rha and UDP-Xyl; UPLC-Q-TOF-MS product analysis
validation_or_evaluation: Standard assay: 50 μL, 100 mM Tris-HCl pH 7.5, 2.5 mM donor, 0.2 mM acceptor, 20 μg protein, 30°C, 1 h; kinetic experiments report three independent replicates but specificity-screen replicate count is not established
main_finding: Source prose substantiates the three Rha×non-substrate zeros and the ten Gal/Xyl donor-specific zeros; protocol context is recoverable for source-level records
limitation_or_gap: No per-cell numeric activities, detection limit or replicate count for the specificity matrix found; do not apply the kinetic-table n=3 to the specificity panel. Binary compilation loses row-specific quantitative uncertainty and has no negative-specific ML ablation.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to assay-negative provenance and context; 2/3 to recovery feasibility; 0/3 direct ML utility

title: A Transcript Profiling Approach Reveals an Abscisic Acid-Specific Glycosyltransferase (UGT73C14) Induced in Developing Fiber of Ligon lintless-2 Mutant of Cotton
domain: Cotton UGT73C14 ABA glycosylation donor/acceptor specificity
research_question: Does recombinant UGT73C14 glycosylate ABA and other tested acceptors across nucleotide-sugar donors?
negative_definition: The compilation contains a UDP-glucuronic-acid×ABA zero; primary text confirms a tested multi-donor panel and reports ABA products with UDP-glucose/UDP-galactose, but does not expose an exact per-cell value or detection threshold for the compiled zero
data_source: Primary PLOS ONE article, Results, Enzyme Assays and Figure S5 caption; three DOI-linked rows in the later Zenodo UGT compilation

title: Negative chemical data boosts language models in reaction outcome prediction
research_question: Can failed-reaction data improve transformer reaction prediction?
negative_definition: RegioSQM20 negative products generated by moving the halogen to an incorrect regioisomer; HiTEA reactions labeled negative when UV-area yield <=1% (threshold selected for this study; low nonzero yields may be included).

title: Leveraging multiple data types for improved compound-kinase bioactivity prediction

Separate prospective profiling of 50 predicted-inactive pairs gave 78% negative predictive value under the paper's <=25% inhibition at 1 µM criterion.
main_finding: Integrating heterogeneous assay readouts expanded training coverage and improved many prediction settings; the study also prospectively assessed inactivity predictions.
limitation_or_gap: Added labels are inferred from assay readouts, not explicit literature-mined negatives. Main gain comparison also increases training data and changes label composition, so it does not isolate an independent causal benefit of negative examples. Prospective NPV is conditional on the selected cohort and assay threshold.
relevance_to_janus: Strong bioactivity precedent for heterogeneous readout integration and experimental validation of predicted inactive pairs; does not solve source-linked historical negative-text recovery or prove the independent gain of recovered negatives.

title: Large scale comparison of QSAR and conformal prediction methods and their applications in drug discovery

The study uses curated records rather than source-text mining and its aggregate pair representation does not preserve full source-measurement provenance.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 2/3: narrows broad novelty and informs censor-aware schema; does not directly establish historical negative extraction or independent model gain.

title: Yield Prediction of Organic Reactions in Biased Data Sets via Positive-Unlabeled Learning
research_question: Can positive-unlabeled learning infer reliable negatives from unlabelled reaction outcomes and improve reaction-yield prediction under simulated reporting bias?
negative_definition: Yield >20% treated as positive for PU classification; lower-yield outcomes function as benchmark negatives. A portion of known negative outcomes from fully labelled HTE sets is hidden to construct positive-unlabelled training data; inferred reliable negatives remain model-generated labels.
data_source: Ahneman Buchwald–Hartwig (3,955), Stevens Ni-borylation (779), Perera Suzuki–Miyaura (5,760), and Neves non-combinatorial Buchwald–Hartwig HTE data (11,328 executed reactions in an ~11.5M candidate space).
method: Spy-based PU learning (PAYN) with CatBoost classifier to identify reliable negatives, followed by yield regression; authors provide an open-source Python framework.
validation_or_evaluation: Authors report the positives-only vs PAYN regression MAE gap narrowed by 61%, 47%, and 33% on three combinatorial HTE sets; Ahneman MAE 11.1% to 6.8%; Perera absolute decrease 1.6%. For Neves, the inferred RN pool reached 97% negative purity under their threshold. These are paper-reported results; not independently reproduced in this audit.
main_finding: Direct, peer-reviewed prior art for addressing missing negative reaction data with PU-inferred negatives and evaluating downstream model value on multiple fully labelled HTE benchmarks; materially rules out a broad cross-molecular-science novelty claim.
limitation_or_gap: The main experiments simulate reporting bias by hiding labels in fully tested HTE matrices; they do not estimate real-world publication missingness or mine explicit negative spans/records from papers. RNs are inferred rather than source-confirmed experimental evidence objects. The >20% outcome threshold is study-specific; effect is reaction-yield-specific and does not establish benefit for protein bioactivity or context/provenance-rich literature recovery. Audit did not independently reproduce code or results.
relevance_to_janus: Relevance 3/3 to bias, inferred-negative recovery and model utility in organic reactions; adjacent but not equivalent to source-linked bioactivity-negative extraction.
